images.filename: Cork and Kinsale from the International Space Station 2013-03-17.jpg
images.caption:
"Cork, Ireland, just visible at the edge of cloud on the coast." – Caption by astronaut Chris Hadfield on board the International Space Station.
This is one of a set of eight pictures of Ireland taken from earth orbit that were posted on the internet by Hadfield to celebrate Saint Patrick's Day in 2013.

The city of Cork near the south coast of Ireland is at the top right of the picture, with the town of Kinsale at bottom left, where the River Bandon flows into the Celtic Sea. The original image has been rotated 90 degrees to the left to present a more familiar orientation.

images.filename: Memorial Garden at the Lusitania Museum & Signal Tower, Old Head, Kinsale.jpg
images.caption: The Memorial Garden at the Lusitania Museum & Signal Tower, Old Head, Kinsale, Ireland. The Cunard passenger liner, RMS Lusitania, bound for Liverpool from New York, sank 12 miles (20 km) away, off the Old Head (the Old Head lighthouse can be seen in the photo at the top right), on 7 May 1915 after being torpedoed by a German U-boat during the First World War. 1198 of the ship's 1959 passengers and crew perished. The ruins of de Courcey castle can be seen in the middle-distance.
images.alt: The Memorial Garden at the Lusitania Museum & Signal Tower, Old Head, Kinsale, Ireland. The Cunard passenger liner, RMS Lusitania, bound for Liverpool from New York, sank 12 miles (20 km) away, off the Old Head (the Old Head lighthouse can be seen in the photo at the top right), on 7 May 1915 after being torpedoed by a German U-boat during the First World War. 1198 of the ship's 1959 passengers and crew perished.
